Subject: Security artifacts request — Dedicated/Private topology and CAIQ mapping

Hi Mateo,

Helios is kicking off an architecture review ahead of our SOC 2 readiness assessment and we need a concise package describing how Redwood isolates Dedicated and Private deployments from the shared control/data planes. Specifically we are asking for: 

- A network topology diagram (single-page preferred) that shows control-plane boundaries, tenant GPU pools, and egress paths for both Hosted/Dedicated and Private (VPC / on-prem) options.
- CAIQ/SIG mapping that highlights which controls are satisfied by the architecture (network isolation, KMS key separation, audit logging, egress filtering).
- A short evidence index listing representative artifacts (design docs, runbooks, diagrams) and who owns them.

Timing: can you provide a preliminary package by EOD Sep 6? If you have a shorter summary first (1–2 pages) that would also be helpful.

A few clarifying points from our auditor: they want to see how the control plane is prevented from routing tenant inference traffic to other tenants, and how KMS/HSM integration works for Private deployments.

Thanks,
Laura

Hi all — attaching the first-pass package for Helios. Notes below; see the attached topology PDF for visuals.

High-level isolation summary (short):
- Control-plane separation: The management/control plane (authentication, model registry, routing policies) runs in a set of control instances logically separated from tenant runtime instances. Control-plane API endpoints are in a management VPC; access to tenant runtimes is strictly via authenticated RPC over mTLS with mutual auth and per-tenant routing tokens.
- Tenant runtime isolation (Dedicated): Dedicated GPU pools provision dedicated node groups for a single customer. Each node group runs in a customer-assigned subnet and has per-tenant KMS key namespace. There is no overlay network that bridges different tenants' runtime subnets.
- Tenant runtime isolation (Private/VPC): For VPC-hosted Private deployments we provide a private control-plane connector; the customer's VPC peering/VPN is limited to an ingress-only data path. Control-plane communications are initiated outbound from the customer's VPC to our management endpoints (no inbound open ports).
- Egress and egress filtering: Egress from runtime instances is forced through a tenant-aware NAT and egress policy engine; outbound destinations are logged and filtered. Default deny is enforced for non-approved destinations.
- KMS/HSM: For Hosted/Dedicated we use per-tenant KMS keys (cloud KMS); for Private on-prem customers we support customer-managed HSM or KMS integration. Cryptographic operations tying model parameters and workspace keys are separated from control-plane key material.
- Audit and logging: Per-tenant audit logs are routed to a write-once store with retention hooks; cross-tenant aggregation is only available to authorized compliance tooling.

Attachments included in this message: topology-priv-dedicated-20280903.pdf (diagram, 3 pages), caiq-mapping-helios-v1.xlsx (CAIQ mapping, tabbed), evidence-index-20280903.csv (list of artifacts and owners).

Quick delivery note: page 2 of the topology PDF contains an air-gapped / on-prem deployment annotation (control-plane relay appliance model). Page 3 is a sequence diagram showing how a request is routed when fallback to a smaller quantized model occurs.

Link to internal delivery folder: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/s/abc123/topology

Let me know if the auditors need a notarized runbook excerpt — Soojin, can you confirm whether we have a signed runbook sample for Helios (ownership: Controls team)?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Network & Security Architect, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Security artifacts request — Dedicated/Private topology and CAIQ mapping

Kim / Mateo — this looks good, thanks for the rapid turnaround. Two follow-ups from our auditor: 

1) KMS/HSM: can you provide a short note (1 paragraph) that explains the customer-managed HSM integration flow for Private on-prem deployments (how keys are provisioned, who holds key material, and whether any key material is exported back to Redwood).

2) Evidence for control-plane separation: the auditor asked for one example artifact (redacted) that shows the control-plane ACL and routing policy applied during a canary deploy. If you have an excerpt of a runbook or a policy file we can accept a redacted copy.

If you can give an ETA for those two items (ideally within 3 business days) that would keep us on schedule for our Sep 15 readiness milestone.

Thanks again — I will share the package with our auditor once we have the two clarifications.

Best,
Laura
